ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=36^\circ$. With $C$ as the center and $CA$ as the radius, the circle intersects $AB$ at point $D$ and $BC$ at point $E$. What is the degree measure of the central angle opposite to the arc $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CD, as shown in the diagram: \\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=36^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A=90^\circ-\angle B=54^\circ$,\\
$\because$ CA=CD,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CDA=\angle A=54^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD=180^\circ-54^\circ-54^\circ=72^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCE=90^\circ-\angle ACD=18^\circ$,\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{18^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, C is near the lower right, AC is a vertical line segment, BC is a horizontal line segment, therefore ∠ACB is a right angle. The circle with C as the center passes through A, and intersects the hypotenuse AB at D, and intersects the direction of the ray/line segment BC at E. D is on AB, E is on BC; the central angle subtended by arc DE is ∠DCE. Reasoning: It is known that ∠ACB = 90°, ∠B = 36°, so ∠A = 180° - 90° - 36° = 54°. Because C is the center of the circle, CA is a radius, and D is on the circle, so CA = CD. Thus △ACD is an isosceles triangle, and AD is collinear with AB, so ∠CAD = ∠A = 54°, hence ∠CDA = 54°. Therefore ∠ACD = 180° - 54° - 54° = 72°. Also because CE is along CB, and ∠ACB = 90°, so ∠DCE = 90° - ∠ACD = 90° - 72° = 18°. Therefore the central angle subtended by arc DE is 18°.
